research_records.raw_claim: Gulzar, Zhu, Han, Perception and Practices of Differential Testing, ICSE-SEIP 2019, DOI 10.1109/ICSE-SEIP.2019.00016; large Google practice study; diff testing supplements unit testing and has cost/noise/sampling challenges.
research_records.status: Published conference paper; primary PDF opened and citation/DOI confirmed. The PDF describes an empirical practice study, not a causal comparative efficacy trial.
research_records.support: Supports matched-input comparisons as supplementary evidence, lack of a full oracle, and risks from noisy outputs and differencing/sampling. Google-scale practice evidence does not show provider agreement establishes correctness or predict these local regressions.
research_records.disposition: Retain, qualified. Decision use: exact contract assertions plus matched comparisons with executable/provider/input identity.

research_records.raw_claim: Graves et al., An Empirical Study of Regression Test Selection Techniques, ACM TOSEM 10(2), 2001; selective test reuse has program/change/suite-dependent cost and fault-detection trade-offs.
research_records.status: Published ACM journal paper; author-hosted full primary PDF opened; bibliographic identity confirmed.
research_records.support: Paper is an empirical comparison of five techniques. Broad conditional trade-off framing is supported. The reported ‘60% at median’ figure was not independently extracted from the returned open excerpt and should remain attributed to the original scout pending a pinpoint check.
research_records.disposition: Retain as conditional background, not a local selection rule or required-coverage reduction.

research_records.raw_claim: Di Nardo et al., STVR 25(4), 2015, DOI 10.1002/stvr.1572; selection savings under 2%, minimization 79.5% with fault-detection loss.
research_records.status: Peer-reviewed published journal article confirmed by University of Limerick publication record. Abstract/record only; verifier did not open full text.
research_records.support: The record's abstract gives <2% selection savings and 79.5% minimization with fault-detection capability above 70%; this is one industrial system and explicitly a trade-off.
research_records.disposition: Retain as counterexample to assuming systematic selection pays off; do not use for dropping this task's required cases.
